# How to Merge Last Two Commits in Git

You can combine (squash) the last two commits into one using **interactive rebase**.

## Quick Method

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

This opens an editor showing your last 2 commits:

```
pick abc1234 First commit message
pick def5678 Second commit message
```

**Change `pick` to `squash` (or `s`) on the second line:**

```
pick abc1234 First commit message
squash def5678 Second commit message
```

Save and close. You'll then be prompted to edit the combined commit message.

---

## Alternative: Soft Reset Method

```bash
# Reset to 2 commits back, keeping changes staged
git reset --soft HEAD~2

# Create a new commit with all changes
git commit -m "New combined commit message"
```

---

## Quick One-Liner

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~2 && git commit --edit -m"$(git log --format=%B --reverse HEAD..HEAD@{1})"
```

---

## ⚠️ Important Notes

| Situation | Recommendation |
|-----------|----------------|
| **Already pushed** | Avoid, or use `git push --force` (risky for shared branches) |
| **Local only** | Safe to do |
| **Shared branch** | Communicate with your team first |

---
